</speech>

<speech by="#krige">

<from><span class="col_2241-2242" refersTo="page_1130"/>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">C. J. KRIGE</person> (Caledon)</from>

<p>seconded.</p>

<p>Agreed to.</p>

<p>Some other additional amendments having been agreed to,</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_agriculture">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE</person></from>

<p>moved: That the Bill be now read a third time.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#vosloo">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">J. A. VOSLOO</person> (Somerset)</from>

<p>objected, whereupon</p>

<p>The third reading was set down for Wednesday.</p>

</speech>

</debateSection>

<debateSection name="#the_railway_budget">

<heading>THE RAILWAY BUDGET</heading>

<speech by="#walton">

<from>Sir <person refersTo="hansard_za">E. H. WALTON</person> (Port Elizabeth, Central)</from>

<p>moved that order No. 3 (Railway Budget Debate) be discharged, his reason being that it was almost impossible to discuss the railway policy of the Government until they had the constructive policy before them.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_railways_and_harbours">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF RAILWAYS AND HARBOURS</person></from>

<p>thought the motion somewhat unreasonable. The proper time to discuss the expenditure which the hon. member referred to would be when the Loan Bill was before the House. He was willing, however, to meet the hon. member, and would move that order No. 3 be discharged, and set down for Wednesday.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#wilcocks">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">C. T. M. WILCOCKS</person> (Fauresmith)</from>

<p>seconded.</p>

<p>The motion was agreed, to.</p>

</speech>

</debateSection>

<debateSection name="#habitual_criminals_bill">

<heading>HABITUAL CRIMINALS BILL</heading>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person></from>

<p>moved that orders 4 up to, and including, No. 10, be discharged for the purpose of taking No. 11 (Habitual Criminals Bill).</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#merriman">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">J. X. MERRIMAN</person> (Victoria West)</from>

<p>said he did not actually want to object to this specially, but he must point out the gravity of such procedure, which had unfortunately grown to be a practice. It was clearly evident to hon. members that there was little chance of their reading the Habitual Criminals Bill that day, and yet they were asked to suspend half a dozen orders and take this Bill. This was a most inconvenient procedure, and they would have to adopt some rule to prevent this sort of thing.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_justice">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF JUSTICE</person>:</from>

<p>I quite appreciate the remarks of the right hon. gentleman, and will withdraw my motion.</p>

</speech>

</debateSection>

<debateSection name="#native_labour_regulation_bill_in_committee">

<heading>NATIVE LABOUR REGULATION BILL.<br/>IN COMMITTEE.</heading>

<speech by="#creswell">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">F. H. P. CRESWELL</person> (Jeppe)</from>

<p>said this was a very important matter, and he would like to know whether it should not be withdrawn, and set down for some other day.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_native_affairs">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF NATIVE AFFAIRS</person>:</from>

<p>I cannot agree to the suggestion.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#merriman">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">J. X. MERRIMAN</person> (Victoria West)</from>

<p>said they had a report from the Select Committee on this Bill, which contained very valuable matter, and ought to be discussed in the House, because they would not be able to discuss it in committee.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_native_affairs">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF NATIVE AFFAIRS</person>:</from>

<p>If my right hon. friend means that he wishes a day for the discussion of the report, I am quite prepared to agree to that.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#mentz">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">H. MENTZ</person> (Zoutpansberg)</from>

<p>moved in line 16, after &#x201C;labourers,&#x201D; to insert &#x201C;not being one of such native labourers &#x201D;; in line 40, to omit &#x201C;or to act as a messenger in connection with the recruiting of labour.&#x201D; He pointed out that many small recruiters despatched then natives without a conductor. One of the natives had a note stating that he was the conductor, but that was not a bona fide way of carrying out the law.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_native_affairs">

<from>&#x2020;The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF NATIVE AFFAIRS</person></from>

<p>said he could not understand the amendment. The definition of &#x201C;conductor&#x201D; included anyone appointed as such by the recruiter, black or white.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#mentz">

<from>&#x2020;Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">H. MENTZ</person> (Zoutpansberg)</from>

<p>said the Bill was so full of pitfalls that a native labour agent would be a lucky man if he did not get into gaol over it. (Laughter.)</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_native_affairs">

<from>&#x2020;The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF NATIVE AFFAIRS</person></from>

<p>did not think the amendment of Mr. Mentz would carry out the object of the mover.</p>

<p>The amendment in line 16 was negatived.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_native_affairs">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF NATIVE AFFAIRS</person></from>

<p>moved: In line 19, to omit all the words after &#x201C;runners&#x201D; to &#x201C;supply&#x201D; in line 2C. and to substitute &#x201C;recruits&#x201D;.</p>

<p>Agreed to.</p>

</speech>

</debateSection>

<debateSection name="#employer&#x201D;_defined">

<heading>&#x201C;EMPLOYER&#x201D; DEFINED.</heading>

<speech by="#minister_of_native_affairs">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF NATIVE AFFAIRS</person></from>

<p>stated that at a later stage he would move an amendment as to the definition of &#x201C;employer.&#x201D; This matter was a delicate one.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#mentz">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">H. MENTZ</person> (Zoutpansberg)</from>

<p>objected to the definition of &#x201C;director,&#x201D; in order to call attention to the enormous powers to he enjoyed by that gentleman. He could grant, renew, or refuse a licence, and he could order an inquiry to be held in the case of any labour agent, and if thought desirable, could cancel the licence. The official&#x2019;s powers would not be confined to recruiting for the mines, but for other kinds of work, such as brick or road making. If a person appealed against any of the director&#x2019;s orders, one had to deposit &#x00A3;50, and if any part of his decision were upheld, the appellant would have to pay all costs. The director had more powers than the Supreme Court.</p>

<p>The definition was agreed to.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#madeley">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">W. B. MADELEY</person> (Springs)</from>

<p>suggested that the Bill should be allowed to stand over until the Minister was prepared to define exactly who and what an employer was.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#merriman">

<from><span class="col_2243-2244" refersTo="page_1131"/>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">J. X. MERRIMAN</person> (Victoria West)</from>

<p>said the Bill had been on the paper for a very long time. It was a Bill to improve a very serious state of affairs, and with the vast amount of work on the paper, there was a serious risk that if this were put off, the Bill would not be passed, and they would lose an opportunity of regulating this whole business, which, he could assure hon. members, was one that cried aloud for regulation. He hoped in the interests of humanity and good government, the Bill would not be postponed.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#creswell">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">F. H. P. CRESWELL</person> (Jeppe)</from>

<p>moved in the definition of runner the word &#x201C;native&#x201D; be omitted, and &#x201C;person&#x201D; substituted. He said he could not see why white men should be prohibited from engaging in this occupation, though he agreed it was not a desirable form of work for white men. Still, when they found the policy of the Government to be such as limited the employment of white men, it was not right that they should shut the door to white men in regard to this occupation.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#merriman">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">J. X. MERRIMAN</person> (Victoria West)</from>

<p>said the hon. member seemed to wish to bring white people down to the low grade of runners. Why they did not wish to have white men as runners was because white men of that class too often went to native kraals, supplied the natives with bad liquor, told them a pack of lies, and engaged them in a, sort of way which made one blush. The sooner that sort of thing was stamped out, the better.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#creswell">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">F. H. P. CRESWELL</person> (Jeppe)</from>

<p>said that so long as the Government were intent on helping to supply natives to do all the bone and muscle work which white men could do, and so refused the white man an opportunity of earning a livelihood, so long would the Labour party object to the white man being prevented, even in his extremity, from earning, in such a way as this, undesirable though it was, at least enough to keep him alive.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#berry">

<from>Sir <person refersTo="hansard_za">W. B. BERRY</person> (Queenstown)</from>

<p>said the object of the Select Committee was to make white men take out labour agents&#x2019; licences. The business of a runner was not one in which they would like to see a white man engaged.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_native_affairs">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF NATIVE AFFAIRS</person></from>

<p>said that Mr. Creswell had often protested, in tones of thunder, against native labour being employed; yet now he wished to make the white man an instrument to procure additional coloured labour.</p>

<p>The amendment of the Select Committee to omit &#x201C;person&#x201D; and to insert &#x201C;native&#x201D; was agreed to.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_native_affairs">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF NATIVE AFFAIRS</person></from>

<p>moved: In line 38, to insert a new definition as follows:; &#x201C;&#x2018; recruiting &#x2019; shall mean the procuring, engaging, or supplying, or the undertaking or attempting to procure, engage, or supply natives for the purposes of employment in work of any kind within or outside the Union.&#x201D;</p>

<p>This amendment, and the amendment proposed by the Select Committee were agreed to.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#mentz">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">H. MENTZ</person> (Zoutpansberg)</from>

<p>moved as an amendment in line 40, after &#x201C;behalf,&#x201D; to omit all the words to the end of the sentence.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_native_affairs">

<from>&#x2020;The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF NATIVE AFFAIRS</person></from>

<p>said that he could not agree with the hon. member that the Bill as it stood might lead to difficulties. A recruit might employ any native on errands.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#venter">

<from>&#x2020;Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">J. A. VENTER</person> (Wodehouse)</from>

<p>supported the amendment.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#grobler">

<from>&#x2020;Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">P. G. W. GROBLER</person> (Rustenburg)</from>

<p>supported the previous speaker. The definition as printed compelled practically every employer to pay a white man for recruiting natives, which was going too far.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#smuts">

<from>&#x2020;General <person refersTo="hansard_za">T. SMUTS</person> (Ermelo)</from>

<p>asked whether natives or coloured people could act as labour agents?</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_native_affairs">

<from>&#x2020;The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF NATIVE AFFAIRS</person></from>

<p>said that no coloured people acted as recruiters.</p>

<p>The amendment was negatived.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#watt">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">T. WATT</person> (Dundee)</from>

<p>asked whether a clause of the Bill had not somehow been dropped out, because the interpretation clause referred to mines and works, and no reference would be found to mines and works, excepting in new clause 24 or old clause 22?</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_native_affairs">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF NATIVE AFFAIRS</person></from>

<p>said that he did not quite follow the hon. member. He did not quite see where the difficulty came in.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#schreiner">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">T. L. SCHREINER</person> (Tembuland)</from>

<p>thought that something was necessary, and must be added, because it seemed that a man needed a licence if he wished to get 20 men to put up a grand stand, for example.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_native_affairs">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF NATIVE AFFAIRS</person></from>

<p>advised the hon. member to wait until they came to clause 5, where the definition came in, and where works were defined; and the same meaning was given to works as in the Mines Bill.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#watt">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">T. WATT</person> (Dundee)</from>

<p>said that he understood that perfectly. The interpretation clause gave certain works certain meanings, because such words were used in subsequent portions of a Bill; but that was not the case in the present Bill, except in the one clause.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#creswell">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">F. H. P. CRESWELL</person> (Jeppe)</from>

<p>said that the intention of the Minister was perfectly clear&#x2014;he wanted to make it as wide as possible.</p>

</speech>

</debateSection>

<debateSection name="#runners&#x201D;_and_europeans">

<heading>&#x201C;RUNNERS&#x201D; AND EUROPEANS.</heading>

<speech by="#duncan">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">P. DUNCAN</person> (Fordsburg)</from>

<p><span class="col_2245-2246" refersTo="page_1132"/>said that, before the clause was put, he would like to ask the Minister whether he was going to provide for a white person who might engage in the work of a runner?</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_native_affairs">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF NATIVE AFFAIRS</person></from>

<p>said that what they proposed was that a European should not be licensed for this work at all. The definition referred to a runner who was a native.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#duncan">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">P. DUNCAN</person> (Fordsburg)</from>

<p>put it whether the effect would not be that a European who engaged in this class of work would be free from all restrictions set out in the Bill, unless there was some positive enactment in the Bill prohibiting a European from carrying out these functions. The definition of &#x201C;runner&#x201D; did not? touch him, nor did any of the restrictions applicable to a runner.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_native_affairs">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF NATIVE AFFAIRS</person></from>

<p>asked the hon. member to read the penalty clause.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#schreiner">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">T. L. SCHREINER</person> (Tembuland)</from>

<p>said that, in view of the questions which had been raised, it seemed to him that the Minister would be well advised if he allowed the clause to stand over.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_native_affairs">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF NATIVE AFFAIRS</person>:</from>

<p>I don&#x2019;t know whether the hon. member desires this Bill to become law; but if he does he is taking a course which will frustrate it.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#creswell">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">F. H. P. CRESWELL</person> (Jeppe)</from>

<p>said that they would like it made dear what was meant by some of these definitions&#x2014;for instance, the portion dealing with advances. Much as they loathed the labour native policy which the Government had adopted, they did not want to see a great deal of the trade of Johannesburg ruined by the introduction of the truck system. Did these advances mean cash or goods and cattle?</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_native_affairs">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF NATIVE AFFAIRS</person></from>

<p>said that the definition meant what it said. There might be advances in cash or any sort of substitute, or anything of value.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#sampson">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">H. W. SAMPSON</person> (Commissioner-street)</from>

<p>said that what they had in their minds was, that employers might compel natives to buy at their own store, instead of in the open market.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#alexander">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">M. ALEXANDER</person> (Cape Town, Castle)</from>

<p>said that, on the second reading debate, he understood the Minister to say that the Government were going to do away with advances by way of cattle. Now, he had told them that they were going to keep that system. &#x201C;Advances,&#x201D; as defined under this clause, would include cattle advances.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_native_affairs">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF NATIVE AFFAIRS</person></from>

<p>said it was not intended that that system should continue, but they must not forget that there were a number of contracts which, may have been made on the basis of that form of advance. The object of the Government was to discountenance the system.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#creswell">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">F. H. P. CRESWELL</person> (Jeppe)</from>

<p>was proceeding to address the committee further when</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#chairman">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">CHAIRMAN</person></from>

<p>ruled him out of order on the ground that he could not discuss details on this clause.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#creswell">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">F. H. P. CRESWELL</person> (Jeppe)</from>

<p>rejoined that his only course, then, would be to divide the House on the clause.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#duncan">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">P. DUNCAN</person> (Fordsburg)</from>

<p>again returned to the question of a European who might engage in the work of a runner, and said he could find nothing in the Bill to prevent a European from acting as a runner or penalising him.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#stockenstrom">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">A. STOCKENSTROM</person> (Heidelberg)</from>

<p>said that if a European engaged in work of that nature, he became a runner, and if he did that work without a licence he be came liable under the Bill.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#chairman">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">CHAIRMAN</person></from>

<p>put the question that the clause as amended stand part of the Bill, and declared that the &#x201C;Ayes&#x201D; had it.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#creswell">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">F. H. P. CRESWELL</person> (Jeppe)</from>

<p>called for a division, which was taken with the following result:</p>

</speech>

<p>Alberts, Johannes Joachim.</p>

<p>Alexander, Morris.</p>

<p>Lemmer, Lodewyk Arnoldus Slabbert,</p>

<p><span class="col_2247-2248" refersTo="page_1133"/>Maasdorp, Gysbert Henry.</p>

<p>Rockey, Willie.</p>

<p>Sauer, Jacobus Wilhelmus.</p>

<p>Schoeman, Johannes Hendrik.</p>

<p>Smartt, Thomas William.</p>

<p>Smuts. Tobias.</p>

<p>Steyl, Johannes Petrus Gerhardus.</p>

<p>Steytler, George Louis.</p>

<p>Stockenstrom, Andries.</p>

<p>Van Niekerk, Christian Andries.</p>

<p>Vermaas, Hendrik Cornelius Wilhelmus</p>

<p>Vintcent, Alwyn Ignatius.</p>

<p>Vosloo, Johannes Arnoldus.</p>

<p>Walton, Edgar Harris.</p>

<p>Watermeyer, Egidius Benedictus.</p>

<p>Watkins, Arnold Hirst.</p>

<p>Watt, Thomas.</p>

<p>Wiltshire, Henry.</p>

<p>The clause as amended was, therefore, agreed to.</p>

<p>On clause 3,</p>

<speech by="#minister_of_native_affairs">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF NATIVE AFFAIRS</person></from>

<p>moved: In line 48, to omit &#x201C;proper officer,&#x201D; and to substitute &#x201C;director.&#x201D;</p>

<p>Agreed to.</p>

<p>On clause 4, labour agents, compound managers, and conductors to be licensed,</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_native_affairs">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF NATIVE AFFAIRS</person></from>

<p>moved an amendment, which would necessitate runners being licensed or obtaining permits.</p>

<p>The amendment was adopted.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#mentz">

<from>&#x2020;Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">H. MENTZ</person> (Zoutpansberg)</from>

<p>moved to add at the end of the clause, &#x201C;and no person shall recruit or aid in recruiting natives on ground leased by him, or in respect of which he collects rents from natives.&#x201D; The object of the amendment was to prevent undue advantage being taken of the natives. At present it often happened that natives who were in arrear with their rent were practically pressed into the service of the mines by the person entitled to collect the rent, which was unfair.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_native_affairs">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF NATIVE AFFAIRS</person></from>

<p>accepted the amendment, which was agreed to</p>

<p>On clause 5, recruiting of native labourers to be under authority of licence,</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_native_affairs">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF NATIVE AFFAIRS</person></from>

<p>moved: In line 10, after &#x201C;engages&#x201D; to insert &#x201C;or recruits.&#x201D;</p>

<p>Agreed to.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#schreiner">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">T. L. SCHREINER</person> (Tembuland)</from>

<p>moved: To add at the end of sub-section (a) &#x201C;ordinary industrial operations or,&#x201D; the object being to render it unnecessary for persons recruiting natives for industrial purposes to take out a licence.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#mentz">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">H. MENTZ</person> (Zoutpansberg)</from>

<p>moved an amendment: In line 10, to omit all the words from &#x201C;bona fide&#x201D; to the end of paragraph (a) and to substitute &#x201C;farming operations, domestic service, trade business, or handicraft, provided the number of natives in his employ do not at any time exceed fifty.&#x201D; He pointed out that as he read the clause, it meant that everybody who engaged natives outside of farming must have a licence.</p>

</speech>

</debateSection>

<debateSection name="#recruiting">

<heading>&#x201C;RECRUITING.&#x201D;</heading>

<speech by="#watkins">

<from>Dr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">A. H. WATKINS</person> (Barkly)</from>

<p>said he did not quite catch the definition of the word &#x201C;recruiting,&#x201D; as it was not on the paper. There were about 1,500 men working on the alluvial diggings; some of these men employed one or two, or perhaps 20 boys, and as be interpreted the clause, they would be compelled to take out a licence. He thought this clause should be recast, so as not to compel these men to take out a licence. He moved to add the following amendment: &#x201C;No person shall recruit natives for employment except for his own behalf.&#x201D;</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#watt">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">T. WATT</person> (Dundee)</from>

<p>hoped the Minister would allow the clause to stand down, because it wanted recasting. According to the construction of this clause it was quite possible to recruit natives for farming or any sort of employment outside the Union. He thought it would be best to delete the words &#x201C;within or outside the Union,&#x201D; and insert the words &#x201C;on any mine or works within or for any purpose whatsoever outside the Union.&#x201D;</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#quinn">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">J. W. QUINN</person> (Troyeville)</from>

<p>thought the clause as it stood was much better than with the amendment of the hon. member (Mr. Watt). There seemed to be some confusion between the word &#x201C;recruiting&#x201D; and &#x201C;employment.&#x201D;</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#watkins">

<from>Dr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">A. H. WATKINS</person> (Barkly):</from>

<p>Could we have a definition of &#x201C;recruiting&#x201D;?</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#quinn">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">J. W. QUINN</person> (Troyeville):</from>

<p>The only accepted definition is where a man went away from his base to recruit labour.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#jagger">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">J. W. JAGGER</person> (Gape Town, Central)</from>

<p><span class="col_2249-2250" refersTo="page_1134"/>said that boys were employed for other purposes than those of the mines. What he wanted to know was if a man engaged a number of boys for work in a store or other work, would be have to take out a licence?</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_native_affairs">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF NATIVE AFFAIRS</person></from>

<p>said it would be extremely difficult to define certain employment. If hon. members would give the Administration credit for a bit of common-sense, he would tell his hon. friend (Mr. Jagger) he could engage his natives provided he did not set up a system of touting.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#runciman">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">W. RUNCIMAN</person> (South Peninsula)</from>

<p>said they had no objection to trusting the Administration, but they did not know what the Administration was. The Minister had just stated that the member for Cape Town could engage as many natives as he wanted provided these men came to him and offered themselves for employment. He (Mr. Runciman) might want 100 men, and would have to send to Cape Town for them. Therefore he came under the operation of this Act. He thought they ought to have the objections stated in this clause. A ship might come in requiring a couple of hundred men; was a stevedore going to take out a licence to supply these?</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#creswell">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">F. H. P. CRESWELL</person> (Jeppe)</from>

<p>said it seemed to him that this Native Labour Bill was simply for the benefit of the mines. The hon. member for Cape Town (Mr. Jagger) and other hon. members were outside its scope altogether. If they were agreed on this point, what could be the objection to the amendment of the hon. member for Zoutpansberg (Mr. Mentz)?</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#chaplin">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">F. D. P. CHAPLIN</person> (Germiston)</from>

<p>said he quite agreed that those people who did not regularly recruit native labourers and did not tout for them should not be included, but he failed to see why farmers or anybody else who recruited labourers for large irrigation works should be excluded. Surely these people should be made to take out licences in the same way as persons engaged in mining and other works. He thought a great deal was to be said in favour of the amendment.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#watt">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">T. WATT</person> (Dundee)</from>

<p>said that the difficulty arose through the omission to describe the nature of the operations or employment in which natives were to be engaged. If the labour was for mines and works, why not say so in the clause? He hoped the Minister would allow the clause to stand down, in order to admit of its being redrafted. At present, it seemed to favour those engaged in farming operations, and so on.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_native_affairs">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF NATIVE AFFAIRS</person></from>

<p>was understood to say that the regulations were to apply to organised recruiting, and he thought it would be better so far as the farming community were concerned, to leave the clause as it was.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#venter">

<from>&#x2020;Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">J. A. VENTER</person> (Wodehonse)</from>

<p>said that the Bill as it stood would prevent even Divisional Councils from engaging gangs of natives to work on roads. He supported the hon. member for Zoutpansberg.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_native_affairs">

<from>&#x2020;The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF NATIVE AFFAIRS</person></from>

<p>said the Bill would be applied to the large industrial areas where they had gold and coal mines. If the amendment of the hon. member for Zoutpansberg were carried, the exemption in favour of agriculture would disappear, and the sole test would be: how many natives does a man employ?</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#watkins">

<from>Dr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">A. H. WATKINS</person> (Barkly)</from>

<p>asked the Minister to give him an assurance that the men working on the River Diggings would not be affected. He pointed out that, as the Bill stood, a farmer might go to a kraal and get natives to dig for him, without taking out a licence; but, if he left his farm and went to dig on the River, unless natives came to him and offered their services, he could not engage them without first taking out a licence.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_native_affairs">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF NATIVE AFFAIRS</person></from>

<p>said that it was not intended to apply the regulations to a case such as had been quoted.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#watt">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">T. WATT</person> (Dundee)</from>

<p>said that, as the clause read now, every employer of native labourers, excepting a farmer, would be required to get a recruiter&#x2019;s licence. The Minister had said that that was not the intention. He thought, the Minister should redraft the clause, so as to make it dear that it only applied to mines and works. He moved that the clause stand over so that the Minister might redraft it.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#mentz">

<from>&#x2020;Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">H. MENTZ</person> (Zoutpansberg)</from>

<p>trusted the Minister would accept the motion because the clause was very important. Agriculture was protected, but other industries should likewise receive assistance.</p>

<p>The motion was agreed to.</p>

<p>On clause 7, discretion as to issue, etc., of all licences,</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#creswell">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">F. H. P. CRESWELL</person> (Jeppe)</from>

<p>said he would like to know on what ground it was proposed to leave it to the will of the Director to say who might or who might not be a labour agent; He maintained that there should be some right to a man to follow the occupation if he thought himself fitted for it. They should not leave it to an official to determine a man&#x2019;s qualification, so long as He bore a good character.</p>

<p>The clause was agreed to.</p>

<p>On clause 8,</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_native_affairs">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF NATIVE AFFAIRS</person></from>

<p>moved: In line 30, after &#x201C;licence&#x201D; to insert &#x201C;applicable to any one district.&#x201D;</p>

<p>Agreed to.</p>

<p>On clause 9,</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_native_affairs">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF NATIVE AFFAIRS</person></from>

<p>moved: In line 61 after &#x201C;licence&#x201D; <span class="col_2251-2252" refersTo="page_1135"/>to insert &#x201C;Provided that the runner may exercise his calling in any additional district if (authorised there to as prescribed.&#x201D;</p>

<p>Agreed to.</p>

<p>On clause 11, circumstances under which licences may be suspended or cancelled,</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#mentz">

<from>&#x2020;Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">H. MENTZ</person> (Zoutpansberg)</from>

<p>moved an amendment to the effect that Magistrates, after hearing cases in connection with contravention of the regulations, should submit all papers to the Director, the latter to have power to order the licence to be cancelled or suspended. The hon. member said that it would be difficult to do the work contemplated under the Bill without contravening the regulations in some way or other. It was too severe a punishment for a man to lose his licence irrevocably. It was because the clause went too far that he had moved the amendment.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_native_affairs">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF NATIVE AFFAIRS</person></from>

<p>thought that the hon. member had gone too far, and it did not necessarily follow that a man would lose his licence because he had been found guilty of a contravention of the Act. The power was left in the hands of the Minister.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#creswell">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">F. H. P. CRESWELL</person> (Jeppe)</from>

<p>thought it was rather stiff that ta labour agent should have his licence suspended merely for getting into the hands of the police for a minor offence. Of course, what was intended was to put the power in the hands of the Minister. He, later, moved an amendment, in line 20, after the word &#x201C;offence,&#x201D; to insert the following words, &#x201C;while exercising his calling as labour agent, conductor, or runner (as the case may be).&#x201D;</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_native_affairs">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF NATIVE AFFAIRS</person></from>

<p>said that the Minister was, after all, the person responsible to Parliament.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#creswell">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">F. H. P. CRESWELL</person> (Jeppe)</from>

<p>thought that Mr. Burton had not understood the effect of the amendment.</p>

<p>Mr. Mentz&#x2019;s amendment was agreed to.</p>

<p>Mr. Creswell&#x2019;s amendment was negatived.</p>

</speech>

</debateSection>

<debateSection name="#magistrates&#x2019;_powers">

<heading>MAGISTRATES&#x2019; POWERS</heading>

<speech by="#mentz">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">H. MENTZ</person> (Zoutpansberg)</from>

<p>moved as an amendment, to omit the words, &#x201C;may suspend the licence and,&#x201D; in line 37, and to insert &#x201C;or suspension thereof for such period,&#x201D; and to omit &#x201C;or its restoration.&#x201D; The hon. member thought they were put ting too extensive powers in the hands of the Magistrate.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_native_affairs">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF NATIVE AFFAIRS</person></from>

<p>said he hoped the hon. member would not press the amendment.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#creswell">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">F. H. P. CRESWELL</person> (Jeppe)</from>

</speech>

<speech by="#chairman">

</speech>

<debateSection name="#contagious_diseases">

<heading>CONTAGIOUS DISEASES</heading>

<p>On clause 12, Contract of employment form and attestation,</p>

<speech by="#minister_of_native_affairs">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF NATIVE AFFAIRS</person></from>

<p>moved: In line 39, to omit all the words from &#x201C;who engages&#x201D; down to &#x201C;licence&#x201D; in line 41, and to substitute &#x201C;or holder of an employer&#x2019;s licence who recruits natives,&#x201D; and to insert the following new sub-section after line 58, viz. &#x201C;(2) Every native labourer shall be registered to the person on whose behalf he is employed or recruited.&#x201D;</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#wessels">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">D. H. W. WESSELS (Bechuana-Land)</person> moved:</from>

<p>In line 46, after &#x201C;concerned; and,&#x201D; to insert &#x201C;that all recruited native labourers whose contracts are submitted for attestation have been medically examined, and are not suffering from any contagious disease, and any contract or contracts entered into with native labourers afflicted with any such disease shall be considered null and void and &#x201D;. The mover said his object was to prevent natives suffering from syphilis going to the mines.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#merriman">

<from>Mr. <person refersTo="hansard_za">J. X. MERRIMAN</person> (Victoria West)</from>

<p>said he entirely concurred in the scope of the amendment, but it did not go far (enough, because other diseases&#x2014;such as tuberculosis, phthisis, and heart disease&#x2014; should be included. All natives should be medically examined before their contracts were completed. He suggested the follow in amendment: &#x201C;In respect of the contract with any native, proof shall be given to the satisfaction of the attesting officer that the native attested is in sound physical health.&#x201D;</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#smuts">

<from>&#x2020;Geneml <person refersTo="hansard_za">T. SMUTS</person> (Ermelo)</from>

<p>moved as an amendment that no native under the age of 18 years he attested. His object, he said, was to prevent the depletion of the native labour supply for farms owing to Kafirs of tender age being sent to the mines.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#minister_of_native_affairs">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">MINISTER OF NATIVE AFFAIRS</person></from>

<p>hoped Mr. Wessels (would not insist on the amendment.</p>

</speech>

<speech by="#chairman">

<from>The <person refersTo="hansard_za">CHAIRMAN</person></from>

<p>notified that as it was now five minutes to six he would, in compliance with the sessional order, have to report progress.</p>

<p>Progress was reported, and leave obtained to sit again on Wednesday.</p>

</speech>

<heading>EVENING SITTING</heading>
